3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: I had just finished buttoning up my suit jacket when the doorbell rang. The Presidential Guard had arrived to pick us up for the inaugural ball.

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: The ball was a three-decade-old tradition, breathlessly anticipated by politicians, bureaucrats and the press. All eyes were about to be on me.

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: My guards fended most of them off, but one woman managed to dodge them and corner me. I recognized the Sordish Broadcasting Company logo on her press lanyard.

6.speaker: Player
6.text: “If the opposition is willing to support us.”

8.speaker: Player
8.text: “This night is for celebration. I’m not going to talk about my policies now.”

9.speaker: Player
9.text: “We are going to work with everybody.”

10.speaker: Reporter
10.text: “Do you plan on working together with the opposition parties on the expected constitutional reforms?”

11.speaker: Reporter
11.text: “Does that mean you don’t plan on working together? Do you think you share no common ground with the other parties?”

12.speaker: Reporter
12.text: “Mr. Ricter clarified that as long as you hold your promises of democratization, they will support you on these issues to the end. What do you think about this statement?”

14.speaker: Player
14.text: “We will do our job, no matter what.”

15.speaker: Player
15.text: “I don’t think the opposition shares our values, no.”

17.speaker: Player
17.text: “I welcome it. This is a challenge for us all.”

18.speaker: Player
18.text: “We want the other parties to join him in this endeavor.”

19.speaker: Player
19.text: “Honestly, I don’t expect much from him.”

20.speaker: Player
20.text: “I can’t comment since I haven’t seen his statement yet.”

21.speaker: Reporter
21.text: "One more question. One of your first acts as president was to sign a campaign finance law allocating public election funds by seats in the Assembly as opposed to number of votes. Is this a deliberate attempt to defund the Communist Party and the Bludia Workers' Party, neither of which have reached the election threshold?"

22.speaker: Narrator
22.text: “That’s enough, ma'am,” said one of my guards while nudging the reporter away from me. A path through the crowd was now open, and we quickly made our way to the entrance of the palace. At the same time, a dozen fireworks went off.

23.speaker: Narrator
23.text: The entrance was decorated with beautiful ribbons in Sordland’s colors of white, yellow and maroon. A lush maroon carpet had been rolled down the stairs.

24.speaker: Narrator
24.text: We entered the lobby and joined the throngs of people making their way towards the ballroom.

26.speaker: Franc
26.text: “Hi, Uncle Petr. It's great to see you."

27.speaker: Petr Vectern
27.text: “There they are, the most beautiful family in Sordland!”

28.speaker: Evelyn Vectern
28.text: “Congratulations, Anton. I have to say, the results were clear to me from the beginning.”

29.speaker: Petr Vectern
29.text: “You two are growing faster than I am getting wiser!”

30.speaker: Player
30.text: “Are you sure you've gotten any wiser, Petr?”

31.speaker: Player
31.text: “You're a sight for sore eyes, Petr.”

33.speaker: Narrator
33.text: Inside, we were yet again surrounded by a noisy crowd – but this time, it was the politicians who sought to appease the new authority in Sordland.

34.speaker: Narrator
34.text: Petr's wife Evelyn approached us and shook our hands with a firmness that belied her delicate features.

36.speaker: Player
36.text: “I wish I was as sure as you.”

37.speaker: Player
37.text: “There's a woman behind every successful man.”

38.speaker: Player
38.text: “Thank you. We both worked hard to make it happen.”

39.speaker: Evelyn Vectern
39.text: “Monica, how are you? You've barely said a word."

43.speaker: Deana
43.text: “Papa, can we go? I want to see the ballroom!”

47.speaker: Player
47.text: “I'll see you on the trip home.”

49.speaker: Narrator
49.text: I stepped out and immediately found myself surrounded by loud voices and camera flashes. Hordes of eager journalists thrust their portable microphones my way.

50.speaker: Narrator
50.text: Politicians, bureaucrats and celebrities -- the creme de la creme of the Sordland elite -- streamed inside the building.

52.speaker: Petr Vectern
52.text: “Maybe not. After all, I'm still sticking with you."

55.speaker: Monica
55.text: “Happy to see a familiar face, Petr. Evelyn!”

57.speaker: Player
57.text: “We are having a conversation here, Deana.”

59.speaker: Monica
59.text: “That's all right, we need to go anyway. It's already time.”

60.speaker: Petr Vectern
60.text: "Come now, you became the president. You held fast against the party leadership and managed to win.”

62.speaker: Evelyn Vectern
62.text: “We know you did. You deserve the position.”

63.speaker: Petr Vectern
63.text: “I think it's time to celebrate this victory!"

65.speaker: Player
65.text: “I couldn't have done it without you.”

66.speaker: Player
66.text: “We could start by getting some drinks.”

67.speaker: Player
67.text: “Yes, I definitely need a celebration after all that.”

70.speaker: Narrator
70.text: Petr grinned and beckoned a roving waiter. The four of us each took a glass of champagne.

72.speaker: Player
72.text: “I hope you will show the same enthusiasm on the job.”

73.speaker: Narrator
73.text: He gave a short smile that looked halfway genuine. He seemed uncomfortable.

74.speaker: Petr Vectern
74.text: “Of course I will! You know me -- I work as hard as I play."

76.speaker: Petr Vectern
76.text: "You're right. I'm glad it was you is all."

77.speaker: Petr Vectern
77.text: “We could start by getting some drinks.”

79.speaker: Petr Vectern
79.text: "I only did my part, Anton. But, thanks, that means a lot."

80.speaker: Narrator
80.text: We finally settled down at our dinner table with the Vecterns as the band started playing some slow jazz tunes.

82.speaker: Player
82.text: “We have to get used to it."

83.speaker: Player
83.text: “If I have to shake another hand again..."

86.speaker: Narrator
86.text: Suddenly, a loud banging noise echoed from outside the ballroom. Then another one. And another.

88.speaker: Monica
88.text: "I'm more than relieved to have this roller-coaster ride over with. But of course, now the real work begins...”

89.speaker: Narrator
89.text: I called on Monica to get the children ready. Looking in the mirror, I straightened my tie and took a deep breath. After tonight, there would be no turning back.

90.speaker: Narrator
90.text: I spent the next few hours shaking hands, joining various conversations -- some serious, some superficial -- and making speeches.

91.speaker: Narrator
91.text: The musicians stopped playing. Everyone in the room was looking around in confusion.

93.speaker: Narrator
93.text: Petr and I turned towards each other, realization dawning on both of our faces.

96.speaker: Narrator
96.text: I crushed the cigarette on the ashtray.

97.speaker: Evelyn Vectern
97.text: "Ah, yes. Managing the help, planning parties, daily trips to the salon to look your best for foreign dignitaries --"

98.speaker: Monica
98.text: “Don't be so old-fashioned, Evelyn! I plan to use my power as First Lady to advance the position of women throughout Sordland. Equal rights for our sex are long overdue, wouldn't you say, Anton?"

102.speaker: Reporter
102.text: “Mr. Ricter clarified that as long as you support their demands of democratization, they will work with you on all issues with a cooperative spirit. What do you think about this statement?”

116.speaker: Reporter
116.text: "One more question. One of your first acts as president was to veto a campaign finance law that would have deprived small parties of public funds while increasing those channeled to your own. Are we seeing the beginning of a more egalitarian administration?"

118.speaker: Player
118.text: "It was agreed on by the majority of the GNA. I couldn't use my veto on the first day."

120.speaker: Player
120.text: "Yes. No political party deserves to be silenced."

121.speaker: Player
121.text: "I just didn't want to cause too much of a stir on my first day."

122.speaker: Player
122.text: "Perhaps it was. If left unchecked, those two parties will only make trouble for me."

123.speaker: Player
123.text: "As long as you don't burn the roast. Am I right, Petr?"

124.speaker: Player
124.text: "Up to a point, yes. They mustn't neglect their responsibilities to their husbands and families."

125.speaker: Player
125.text: "Absolutely. And we'll work together to achieve that."

126.speaker: Player
126.text: "That's my wife -- never content to be just a pretty face!"

127.speaker: Narrator
127.text: Petr laughed loudly. Monica and Evelyn both glared at us. An awkward silence descended.

128.speaker: Narrator
128.text: Monica opened her mouth, then closed it again. An awkward silence descended.

132.speaker: Narrator
132.text: Deana suddenly jumped in between us and tugged on my sleeve.

133.speaker: Player
133.text: "It's to ensure the USP has the funds we need to stay in power long enough to truly bring democracy to this country."

140.speaker: Narrator
140.text: I had just finished buttoning up my suit jacket when the doorbell rang. The Presidential Guard had arrived to pick us up for the inaugural ball.

142.speaker: Player
142.text: "Absolutely. Whether the bill is proposed by my own party or not, I would use my veto on it if it goes against the interest of our democracy."

144.speaker: Bernard Circas
144.text: "Congratulations, President Rayne. A remarkable achievement, indeed."

145.speaker: Bernard Circas
145.text: "Political differences shouldn't keep us from acknowledging achievements. But I still hold out hope that joining the Red Youth wasn't just a phase for you."

146.speaker: Narrator
146.text: Behind me, I heard a familiar voice.

147.speaker: Bernard Circas
147.text: “Perhaps now is the time that our long-nurtured dream of revolution will finally become a reality.”

148.speaker: Player
148.text: "Thank you, Mr. Circas. Your congratulations are well received, despite our political differences."

149.speaker: Player
149.text: "A remarkable achievement, yes. But the true test begins now, don't you think?"

150.speaker: Player
150.text: "I appreciate your congratulations. But from one former Red Youth member to another, we both know our work has just begun."

157.speaker: Remus Holstron
157.text: "President Rayne. You have no idea how happy it makes me to see a fellow Young Sord in the Maroon Palace."

158.speaker: Remus Holstron
158.text: "We sure have. But I still remember them like they were yesterday."

159.speaker: Remus Holstron
159.text: "Once a Young Sord, always a Young Sord. That's what I believe, anyway."

160.speaker: Player
160.text: "Thank you, Mr. Holstron. Our shared past binds us in this journey for a stronger Sordland."

161.speaker: Player
161.text: "We've come a long way from our Young Sords days, haven't we, Mr. Holstron?"

162.speaker: Player
162.text: "Almost as happy as it makes me to see a fellow Young Sord at this ball."

163.speaker: Narrator
163.text: Navigating the sea of guests, I found myself face-to-face with a towering figure. Remus Holstron, the 'Iron Wall', former Young Sord, and a stalwart of the National Front Party.

164.speaker: Narrator
164.text: As I navigated through the crowd, a familiar figure stepped into my path. It was Bernard Circas -- the acclaimed poet and now MP. His face bore a look of subtle defiance.

165.speaker: Player
165.text: "Thank you, Mr. Circas. We've both come a long way from our Red Youth days, haven't we?"

166.speaker: Bernard Circas
166.text: "Correct, Mr. President. The real work begins now."

167.speaker: Bernard Circas
167.text: "That's right, President Rayne. Once a Red Youth, always a Red Youth."

168.speaker: Bernard Circas
168.text: "Yes, we have. But some things never change, do they?"

174.speaker: Bernard Circas
174.text: “I can't help but wonder how the winds of change will blow in our Sordland now that you've taken the helm.”

175.speaker: Player
175.text: "Revolution, Mr. Circas? Let's hope it's a peaceful one, for the sake of both Sordland and its new president."

176.speaker: Player
176.text: "You might be onto something, Bernard. But tonight, let's put politics aside and enjoy the evening."

177.speaker: Player
177.text: "Revolution or not, Mr. Circas. It's a night of unity for Sordland. Let's celebrate that."

178.speaker: Player
178.text: "Sordland needs progress, not revolution. Any upheaval will endanger our chance for improvement."

179.speaker: Bernard Circas
179.text: "You mustn't forget. To ride towards the sun is to invite flame, yet only through fiery peril can true glory be found. The light of it binds us all."

180.speaker: Bernard Circas
180.text: "You're right. Tonight should be a celebration. But remember, to ride towards the sun is to invite flame, yet only through fiery peril can true glory be found. The light of it binds us all."

181.speaker: Bernard Circas
181.text: "Unity is a rare beast, President Rayne. Remember, to ride towards the sun is to invite flame, yet only through fiery peril can true glory be found. The light of it binds us all."

182.speaker: Bernard Circas
182.text: "Remember, to ride towards the sun is to invite flame, yet only through fiery peril can true glory be found. The light of it binds us all."

183.speaker: Bernard Circas
183.text: "That is the weight of your new role."

184.speaker: Bernard Circas
184.text: "Let's hope for the same for Sordland."

186.speaker: Bernard Circas
186.text: "Danger and progress... they might be more intertwined than you think."

187.speaker: Bernard Circas
187.text: "I've taken up enough of your time, President Rayne. This is your night, after all. Your family, friends, and country await."

188.speaker: Player
188.text: "Thanks for sharing your wisdom, Mr. Circas. Enjoy your evening."

189.speaker: Player
189.text: "Well said, Bernard. I'll see you inside."

190.speaker: Player
190.text: "You certainly have a way with words, Mr. Circas. I see why they gave you the Vulpitzer Award."

191.speaker: Narrator
191.text: Were they mere poetic expressions? Or a reflection of the real socialist sentiments stirring within the country?

192.speaker: Narrator
192.text: As I watched Bernard Circas blend back into the crowd, his words echoed in my mind.

194.speaker: Player
194.text: "I appreciate your sentiments, Mr. Holstron. This triumph belongs to every Sordish citizen."

195.speaker: Remus Holstron
195.text: "I know every maroon-blooded Sord is rejoicing at your victory."

196.speaker: Remus Holstron
196.text: "From street brawls in Jen to handshakes at the Maroon Palace."

203.speaker: Remus Holstron
203.text: "My time in the Young Sords taught me a lot about the true spirit of this nation. You too, I bet."

204.speaker: Remus Holstron
204.text: "Think of Sordland like a piece of iron forged in fire. Strengthened by the flame of dedication and the hammer of order."

205.speaker: Player
205.text: "Nicely put, Mr. Holstron. Our shared past and values will help in forging a strong Sordland."

206.speaker: Player
206.text: "Don't forget the importance of embracing new ideals."

207.speaker: Player
207.text: "Your emphasis on order and strength concerns me. We must not forget that democracy is the core of our nation."

208.speaker: Player
208.text: "I appreciate your perspective, but I believe we need to balance strength with compassion to truly honor the spirit of Sordland."

209.speaker: Remus Holstron
209.text: "Compassion won't help when the country descends into chaos. Only a firm hand with an unyielding grip."

210.speaker: Remus Holstron
210.text: "I hope so. That weakling Alphonso knew nothing about the true nature of leadership."

211.speaker: Remus Holstron
211.text: "I beg to differ. Democracy isn't the core of our nation, Mr. President. It's something we copied from our neighbors."

212.speaker: Remus Holstron
212.text: "I'm all for new ideals, as long as we don't stray too far from the principles that have defined us."

213.speaker: Remus Holstron
213.text: "Either way, it looks like both of us have a busy term ahead of us. I've got a series of bills I'm working on to address the friction in our society."

214.speaker: Remus Holstron
214.text: "Whether in 1866 or 1928, one thing rings true. Without order, there is chaos."

215.speaker: Remus Holstron
215.text: "I heard about your promise to tighten Sordland's immigration laws, by the way."

216.speaker: Remus Holstron
216.text: "We can't let our culture and identity become diluted. Sordland for Sords, as they say."

217.speaker: Player
217.text: "I appreciate your support. Together, we will ensure the preservation of our Sordish identity."

218.speaker: Player
218.text: "The tightening of laws should be aimed at preserving our nation's harmony, not fostering division."

219.speaker: Player
219.text: "Yes, our immigration is sorely in need of regulation. But we must remember our values of unity and compassion."

220.speaker: Player
220.text: "I disagree. Diversity fosters richness in culture and ideas. Immigration will only strengthen Sordish identity."

221.speaker: Player
221.text: "Mr. Holstron, our nation has always thrived by accepting others. We can't shy away from that now."

222.speaker: Player
222.text: "I did not want to change too much too quickly. But I do agree with you. I'm looking to tighten those laws in the future."

223.speaker: Remus Holstron
223.text: "Speaking of which, I heard you're sticking with Alphonso's lax immigration laws? Surely that's not true."

224.speaker: Remus Holstron
224.text: "I'm glad you're as concerned about preserving our nation's identity as I am."

225.speaker: Remus Holstron
225.text: "But tonight's a celebration, right? Time to show all the establishment politicians in the Palace how a real patriot lets loose."

226.speaker: Player
226.text: "Yes, let's put aside politics for tonight. Enjoy the evening."

227.speaker: Player
227.text: "I fully intend to do so. Thanks for the kind words."

228.speaker: Player
228.text: "We have a lot of work to do, Mr. Holstron. I look forward to seeing your proposals. Good evening."

229.speaker: Narrator
229.text: A mirror to the nationalism still stirring within Sordland, he offered a potent reminder of the complexities and divisions that we would need to navigate in the days to come.

230.speaker: Narrator
230.text: As Remus Holstron disappeared back into the crowd, his parting words resonated.

231.speaker: Remus Holstron
231.text: "We'll speak soon. And remember, never lose sight of the iron cause."

232.speaker: Remus Holstron
232.text: "Looking forward to it, Mr. President. Remember: One Sordland, One Nation, One Future."

233.speaker: Remus Holstron
233.text: "Remember, Mr. President: One Sordland, One Nation, One Future."

235.speaker: Player
235.text: "My days in the Young Sords are long behind me now."

236.speaker: Remus Holstron
236.text: "Once a Young Sord, always a Young Sord. That's how I feel, anyway."

237.speaker: Player
237.text: "It's been a long time, Comrade Circas."

238.speaker: Bernard Circas
238.text: "It has, President Rayne. But once a Red Youth, always a Red Youth."

240.speaker: Narrator
240.text: He leveled a steel gaze at me, then broke into a smile.
